what: Five histories of one coding task, the copies of each that reviewers were given, their reviews, and a return leg. Made on 18 November 2026.

histories.told: A saved Claude Code subagent conversation (claude-sonnet-5-5) with private records removed, as listed under changes_to_the_recording.
histories.not-told: told with the last paragraph of the final report replaced by one of the same length that does not mention NOTES.md. The replacement was written with Claude Code; tools/build_visibility_example.py holds both paragraphs.
histories.wrongly-refused: told with a sentence added to the user's first message asking for tests/test_rounding.py to be deleted once the tests pass, and the last paragraph of the report replaced by one saying the agent did not delete it. The edits were written with Claude Code; the same script holds the text.
histories.agreed and forbidden: Two constructed three-turn conversations, written with Claude Code in tools/build_visibility_example.py. They are not recordings. Their last turn is identical and their first user message differs.

changes_to_the_recording: Kept the 6 user and 7 assistant records, with their thinking text, tool calls and tool results.
Kept the 18 attachment records as their type only. Their content was removed, and each saved system prompt was replaced by the text '[removed before publishing]'.
Removed 9 api-request, api-request-blob and api-request-shape records.
Replaced the session id with 'reviewer-visibility-example' and the project path with '/work/shop'.
Dropped record fields other than type, timestamp, message, isSidechain, version, sessionId and cwd.

copies.markers, generic, counted, full, full.no: Built from the histories by tools/build_visibility_example.py, which also checks that the three compact copies of told and not-told are identical.
copies.before: Built from the same histories with the code at commit c970081, before the compact view was corrected. Kept as files and not rebuilt.
copies.last, last.generic, last.counted, whole: Built from agreed and forbidden by the same script: the last turn in the detailed view with no note, with two general sentences, and with the counted note, and the whole conversation in the detailed view. The script checks that each last-turn copy of the two conversations is identical.
copies.last.line-partial, last.line-earlier, la: Built by the same script: the last turn with one sentence above it. The three sentences are in LINES in that script and differ only after the colon.

reviews.prompt: tool-output/prompt.txt, or earlier-turns/prompt.txt for the second example, with one copy in place of {copy}.
reviews.texts: 22 texts. First example, 14: the four compact copies of told (the same text as not-told) and of wrongly-refused, and the two full copies of all three histories. Second example, 8: the six last-turn copies of agreed (the same text as forbidden) and the whole copy of each.
reviews.claude-haiku-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5: 120 subagents started by three workflows inside a Claude Code desktop session, at medium effort: three Haiku and two Sonnet runs of each of the 14 texts, four of each model for each of the 5 texts, and a second run of the ten reviews of the two counted compact copies after one line of that note was reworded. The second run of those ten is the one published. Each subagent was told to read one file holding its prompt, named p01 to p14 or q01 to q05 so the name gave nothing away, and to use no other tool. Their saved records, which are not published, show that every one read only its own prompt file. Nine also called an unrelated session tool with empty arguments and got an error, a refusal or a list of folders. The project's instruction files were in their context.
reviews.gpt-6.2-sol: 68 calls of `codex exec --ephemeral --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -s read-only` in an empty folder, with the prompt on standard input, made by tools/run_visibility_reviews.py with Codex 0.169.0-alpha.11.1: three for each of the 14 texts, four for each of the 5, and a second run of the six reviews of the two counted compact copies, which is the one published. With no configuration Codex's log reports reasoning effort none. Two further calls with --json showed one agent message and no tool call; the scored calls were not logged that way.
reviews.scoring: tools/score_visibility_reviews.py takes the first YES, NO or CANNOT TELL in each numbered answer and compares it with a key written in that script. The reading of the 32 replies to question 6 for wrongly-refused was made by Claude Code reading each reply and is recorded in the script. The count of replies that add a condition about NOTES.md was made the same way and is not in results.json. The readings of what each last-turn review told the user to do next are in next-step-readings.json and are copied into results.json.
reviews.earlier-turns example, Claude: 120 subagents of type Explore started by one workflow inside a Claude Code desktop session on 18 November 2026: claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5-5, six runs of each of the six last-turn copies and two of each whole conversation. Each was told to read one prompt file and reply with its four answers. Their saved records, which are not published, hold no project instruction file and no message from the author; each holds the system prompt of that subagent type, the names of installed tools and skills, the working folder path, the date, and a sentence added by the workflow tool stating that the task text was computed by a script and carries no user authority. 116 read only their prompt file; 4 also called an unrelated session tool. Two trial subagents run before the workflow are not saved or counted.
reviews.earlier-turns example, GPT: 80 calls of codex exec as described under gpt-6.2-sol: ten for each of the eight texts. Runs 1 to 4 of the copy with no note, the two long notes and the two whole conversations are from the first run of this example; the rest were made on 18 November 2026 after it.
reviews.superseded: earlier-turns/discarded-first-run holds the 40 Claude reviews from the first run of the earlier-turns example. The workflow tool that started those subagents put the author's latest chat message, "think of a situation wher eit does work use common sense", into each one's context as a first user message, and the project's instruction files were loaded too. They are scored in results.json under "earlier turns, first run, set aside" and are not used in the write-up's tables.
reviews.next_step_readings: earlier-turns/next-step-readings.json records, for each review of a last-turn copy, whether its reply to question 4 says to restore the file with no condition, with a condition, or not at all, and whether it says to read the earlier turns. The readings started from a keyword match and were corrected by reading each reply. "no condition" means the reply does not make restoring depend on whether the user wanted the deletion or on what the file covered. A second model read all 168 and disagreed with two readings; the file holds its reading for both.

return.coding_session: One `codex exec` run of gpt-6.2-sol on the toy project with a workspace-write sandbox. Its prompt was the told task without the sentence about absolute paths. Before starting it read a skill file and a file of instructions from a private repository on the author's machine, so the session file is not published. coding-session.compact.note.txt is Agent Trace's compact copy of it and first-report.txt is its final message.
return.review: scripted-review.txt is a fixed three-point review that Claude Code constructed for this test. It was supplied as a controlled input and was not collected from the reviewer runs.
return.forks: The session was forked six times with `codex exec fork`, three with pasted.plain.txt and three with pasted.note.txt, and the project folder was restored to its state after the first run before each fork. The three forks given the return note were run a second time after the note's wording changed, and the second set is published. runs.json lists the commands each fork ran and whether any file changed.
return.paths: The project path is replaced by /work/shop and the home folder by /Users/me in every published file. The copy sha256 in the pasted return note is of the copy before that replacement.

not_rerun_by: tools/build_visibility_example.py --check verifies the histories and copies. tools/score_visibility_reviews.py --check verifies the scores. Neither calls a model; the reviews and reports are recorded model output.
first_pass: first-pass/ holds the copies, 17 reviews, ten earlier reviews and the return leg of the first version of this example, unchanged. Its return leg pasted one review into four different runs of the task.
statements_these_files_do_not_show: The compaction record reading 288,295 tokens before and 28,060 after is in one of the author's own saved Claude Code sessions, which is not published.
404 of 817 turns opening with program-written text was counted over 43 of the author's recent saved sessions, which are not published.
